newsitem.title: UK: Grand Met/Guinness see no regulatory snags.
newsitem.headline: Grand Met/Guinness see no regulatory snags.

text.p: British based food and drinks companies Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness said on Monday they do not expect to face any regulatory hurdles to their 20 billion pound($32.5 billion) merger.

Joint chairman George Bull said he did not expect the merger to face any problems with the regulatory authorities, as the joint spirits business would give the group less than 10 percent of the world's accessible spirits market.
"We are entirely confident that we will be able to obtain the agreement of the regulatory authorities both here in Europe and also in the United States and elsewhere," he said.
Bull said the companies had studied the regulatory requirements carefully. "(We) would not be here if we were not entirely confident we could satisfy those requirements," he added.

GrandMet's portfolio includes white spirits - J&B, Smirnoff vodka, Bailey's, Malibu and Cinzano while Guinness is mainly in brown spirits like Johnnie Walker whisky and Bell's. GrandMet brands are dominant in Europe whereas Guinness is much stronger in the Far East.
GrandMet owns food business Pilsbury in North America and Burger King while Guinness' other main business is brewing stout.
